subject: Renewal + expansion: proposed usage+reserve hybrid and onboarding milestones
messages:
From: Nora Patel <ops@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -0000
Subject: Renewal thoughts — moving to hybrid usage + reserve

Soojin,

Hope you're well. We're starting our internal renewal discussions and want to explore switching from an annual committed model to a hybrid approach: a smaller reserved commitment for baseline latency guarantees + usage-based capacity for spikes. Our goals are:
- Reduce overcommit costs during slower months
- Keep predictable baseline SLAs for latency-critical features
- Have a clear ramp plan for Q1–Q3 next year as we expand features to new teams

Can Redwood sketch a proposal (pricing and operational playbook) that includes a phased ramp, co-terming options across subsidiaries, and any onboarding milestones required to get private deployment ready? Procurement looped in (cc).

Thanks,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Platform Ops | Nimbus Analytics

Nora — thanks for the clear ask, appreciate the context.

Quick summary of what I think will align with your goals:
- Baseline reserved commit sized for 30–40% of peak Q3 usage (keeps latency SLO solid)
- Usage tier that charges per 1k tokens beyond commit with an aggressive post-commit volume discount at defined thresholds
- Ramp schedule in three phases (pilot, scale, enterprise) tied to onboarding milestones and canary windows
- Optional co-terming across subsidiaries with centralized billing + per-subsidiary usage reporting

I attached a short proposal that shows pricing slices and a 10-week onboarding checklist — includes a private agent option if you need VPC isolation. I'll pull in pricing specifics from Karthik and attach a DocuSign-ready term sheet once we align on commit size.

Next step: can we set a 30-minute sync on Friday to run numbers? Proposed slot: Fri 11:00–11:30 PT.

Best,
Soojin Lee

> Nora — thanks for the clear ask...

Thanks — adding some concrete pricing math so we have a crisp proposal for Friday's sync. Key points:
- Reserved tier A (baseline): $X/month for reserved capacity equivalent to 40% of projected peak Q3 token throughput. This includes guaranteed latency SLO and dedicated KV-cache warmup.
- Usage overage: $Y per 1k tokens with a volume ladder: 0–50M tokens: Y; 50–200M: Y*0.85; 200M+: Y*0.70.
- Ramp credits: if Nimbus hits the scale phase within 90 days, we provide a one-time credit equal to 10% of baseline reserved spend to offset onboarding work.

Operational notes: Dedicated pool size changes require 7 business days notice for guaranteed SLO; autoscaling bursts can be configured for immediate but best-effort capacity at a slightly higher usage rate.

I'll bring a draft term sheet to the call. If procurement needs specific legal language about data retention or SOC 2 scoping, let me know ahead of time so Legal can prep.

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Nora — adding the customer success perspective and a proposed onboarding cadence.

We recommend a three-phase rollout that maps directly to your internal milestones:
Phase 1 — Pilot (Weeks 0–4)
- Validate integration with 2 product teams
- KV cache warmup, prefix caching rules, and latency smoke tests
- Success criteria: <100ms p50 on sample requests and no regression in prompt fidelity check suite

Phase 2 — Scale (Weeks 5–8)
- Expand to 6 additional teams, enable autoscaling bursts, observed SLOs for 30 days
- Conduct a dry-run failover to dedicated fallback model

Phase 3 — Enterprise (Weeks 9–10)
- Full rollout, enable co-terming billing aggregation, and hand-off to your platform ops team

I'll own the 10-week onboarding checklist and weekly checkpoint calls. Attaching the XLS with milestones and owner columns. If you want a playbook tailored to each subsidiary (for co-terming), we can scope that in week 1.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
